title: The $\ell$-adic trace of the projective line and the integration identities
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and work with separated finite-type schemes over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$, in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. All schemes below are Noetherian. For each such scheme $T$, write $A_{n,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_T$ for the constant finite coefficient sheaf and $A_{\bullet,T}=(A_{n,T})_{n\ge1}$ with quotient transitions. The derived category of inverse systems means the ordinary derived category of strict towers of sheaves of $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-modules, as in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]. Finite twists, their compatible transitions, and integral twists are those of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. Write $\Zl_T=\varprojlim_n A_{n,T}$ for the completed coefficient sheaf, identified with the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaf by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]; it is distinguished from $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. The trace and identities below concern completed coefficients.

Let $q:\mathbf P^1_Y\to Y$ be the projection, let $p_1,p_2$ be the two
projections of $W=\mathbf P^1_Y\times_Y\mathbf P^1_Y$, and let $\delta_{\Zl}$ be
the morphism of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit].

1. In the derived category of inverse systems on $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the unit
   and the class of a section give an isomorphism
   $\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet\oplus\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet$.
   Twisting by $(1)[2]$, projecting onto the second summand and applying
   $R\varprojlim$ defines a $\Zl$-linear trace
   $\operatorname{Tr}_q:Rq_*\Zl(1)[2]\to\Zl$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Zl)$ whose
   reductions are the torsion traces of [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology]. The same
   construction over $\mathbf P^1_Y$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i}$.
2. For $i=1,2$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i}\circ Rp_{i*}(\delta_{\Zl})=1_{\Zl}$ in
   $D((\mathbf P^1_Y)_{\mathrm{proét}},\Zl)$, where $Rp_{i*}\Delta_*\Zl=\Zl$.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$. The first-Chern-class construction of [det-sp-tower-classes](2), specialized to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $L=\mathcal O_P(1)$, supplies a single morphism of varying-coefficient derived systems, not merely a compatible family in the individual derived categories. Use its adjoint and the unit to form $b_\bullet=(1,h_\bullet)$. For the standard section $s=[1:0]:Y\hookrightarrow P$, its image has equations $t_0=x_1/x_0$ on $U_0=(x_0\ne0)$ and $t_1=1$ on $U_1=(x_1\ne0)$. The generators $e_i=t_i^{-1}$ of its Cartier line bundle satisfy $e_0=(x_0/x_1)e_1$ on the overlap, which is the transition of $\mathcal O_P(1)$. Thus $\mathcal O_P(s(Y))=\mathcal O_P(1)$.

source.place: paragraph (1), construction of (1,h_bullet) and levelwise cone argument

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$, apply [sk-lem-geo-cartier] with $Z=P$, $D=s(Y)$, $r=n$, and $R=\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. This is a finite commutative $R$-algebra; $\ell$ is invertible on $P$. The section is effective Cartier: $x_1/x_0$ is the polynomial coordinate on $U_0$, hence a non-zero-divisor over any base ring, and its ideal is the unit ideal on $U_1$. The cited theorem uses the ordinary small pro-etale module category and the finite line $\nu_P^*(\mu_{\ell^n}\otimes_{A_{n,P}}A_{n,P})$. The canonical tensor-unit isomorphism $z\otimes a\mapsto az$ identifies this with $\nu_P^*\mu_{\ell^n}=A_{n,P}(1)$, so both the coefficient category and the target of its Cartier morphism are exactly the ones used here. Extension from $R$ to $\Lambda=R$ is the identity scalar-extension functor under that same tensor-unit identification. Its composite with the restriction unit is the Kummer boundary of the generator torsor of $\mathcal O_P(s(Y))=\mathcal O_P(1)$, so it is the evaluated Chern class used in $b_n$. This agrees with the positive Cartier normalization $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$ recorded in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]. This invocation is only at finite levels: the coherent system morphism itself was supplied by [det-sp-tower-classes](2), not inferred from equality of finite-level derived morphisms.

source.place: paragraph (1), construction of (1,h_bullet) and levelwise cone argument

proof.text: Exactness and cohomology in the varying-coefficient system category are levelwise by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Evaluation of derived direct image is levelwise by [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison], including its unit. At level $n$, [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology] with $r=n$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ identifies $b_n$ as an isomorphism. The cone of $b_\bullet$ therefore has every cohomology system zero, so $b_\bullet$ is an isomorphism. Finally restrict scalars from the ring system $A_\bullet$ to the constant system $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$; restriction is exact, since kernels and cokernels keep their underlying groups. The canonical direct-image comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied on the tower topoi also to these restriction-of-scalars morphisms, identify the resulting map with the asserted map in the constant-coefficient tower category. No faithfulness of derived evaluation is used.

source.place: paragraph (1), construction of (1,h_bullet) and levelwise cone argument

proof.text: The twisting and second-summand projection in [det-sp-tower-classes](4), for $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, give the system trace $t_{q,\bullet}$. Concretely the twisted isomorphism has source $A_{\bullet,Y}(1)[2]\oplus A_{\bullet,Y}$ and target $Rq_*A_{\bullet,P}(1)[2]$; compose its inverse with $\operatorname{pr}_2$. This is the twist of the map just constructed, with the inverse-image/direct-image projection identification built into that cited splitting. Its evaluation is the projection defining the finite trace in [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology], because evaluation preserves composition, inverses, units and the prescribed twisting construction. The same construction applies to $p_1,p_2$, which are projective lines over $P$. Thus all three traces are morphisms of systems before taking a limit.

source.place: paragraph (1), twisting the splitting and defining the trace on systems

proof.text: Write $C_T=\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ and $R_T=\Zl_T$. For the coefficient tower the quotient maps are epimorphisms; for its twist the maps are epimorphisms by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](1). Therefore [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic], with ring sheaf $C_T$, identifies $R\varprojlim A_{\bullet,T}=R_T$ and $R\varprojlim A_{\bullet,T}(1)=R_T(1)$, for $T=Y,P,W$. The latter also identifies the transition maps with the roots-of-unity power maps. Apply $R\varprojlim$ to $t_{q,\bullet}$. The canonical natural comparison [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], applied with constant coefficient sheaves $C_P,C_Y$, identifies the resulting source with $Rq_*\operatorname{Res} R_P(1)[2]$ and the target with $\operatorname{Res} R_Y$. It commutes with all tower projections. This is a trace over the discrete constant ring at this point. The completed coefficient identification is [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: paragraph (1), applying Rlim and identifying the source and target; Stacks 0A07

proof.text: We now obtain the asserted completed-coefficient trace and check its reductions as actual morphisms. The source coefficient line $R_P(1)$ is derived complete and has derived reduction $A_{n,P}(1)$ by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](4). The target $R_Y$ is also derived complete: its ordinary reductions are $A_{n,Y}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], its derived reductions are ordinary since it is the free rank-one module over itself, and the preceding epimorphic-tower limit computation identifies its canonical completion unit with an isomorphism. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] in its completed-coefficient categories to $R_P(1)[2]$; it makes $Rq_*R_P(1)[2]$ complete. Its coefficient-datum hypotheses for $(\mathbf Z_\ell,(\ell))$ hold: [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] gives the finite perfect quotients, and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](2), with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, makes $\mathbf Z_\ell$ a principal ideal domain. Every ideal is therefore generated by one element, which is the Noetherian condition.

source.place: paragraph (1), completeness, completed linearity and finite reduction; Stacks 099N, 093M, 099I

proof.text: Restriction to constant coefficients commutes with derived direct image by the ringed-topos composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The equivalence [sk-lem-integral-models](1), with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, therefore lifts the trace of step 5 uniquely to $\operatorname{Tr}_q:Rq_*R_P(1)[2]\to R_Y$.

source.place: paragraph (1), completeness, completed linearity and finite reduction; Stacks 099N, 093M, 099I

proof.text: The finite-reduction and limit-unit comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], together with the projection-compatible finite-reduction isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], identify its reduction with $t_{q,n}$. Indeed the square for $R\varprojlim t_{q,\bullet}$ and the $n$th tower projections commutes by naturality; the derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction], with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, identifies a projection to level $n$ with its finite-reduction adjoint. Under the finite-reduction comparisons above this adjoint is exactly the reduced map, and the just cited comparisons identify the two adjoints with $t_{q,n}$. By step 4 this is the torsion trace of [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology]. This argument also applies to $p_1,p_2$.

source.place: paragraph (1), completeness, completed linearity and finite reduction; Stacks 099N, 093M, 099I

proof.text: Let $c_\bullet$ be the system diagonal class of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](4), and form $e_{i,\bullet}=t_{p_i,\bullet}\circ Rp_{i*}c_\bullet$ after the canonical source identification $Rp_{i*}\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P}=A_{\bullet,P}$. This identification follows from $p_i\Delta=\mathrm{id}_P$ and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The replacement of $R\Delta_*$ by $\Delta_*$ is justified by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact]: the diagonal is the closed Cartier divisor cut out by $x_0y_1-x_1y_0$, and its complement is quasi-compact since $W$ is Noetherian. Apply this exactness first in the category of varying-coefficient systems $A_\bullet$: kernels and cokernels are levelwise by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], so $\Delta_{A,*}$ is exact there and $R\Delta_{A,*}A_{\bullet,P}=\Delta_{A,*}A_{\bullet,P}$. Let $U_T$ be restriction from $A_{\bullet,T}$-modules to towers of $C_T=\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-modules. It is exact on underlying sheaves. The equality of underived composites $U_W\Delta_{A,*}=\Delta_{C,*}U_P$, together with the ringed-topos composition comparison just cited, gives $R\Delta_{C,*}A_{\bullet,P}=U_W\Delta_{A,*}A_{\bullet,P}=\Delta_*A_{\bullet,P}$. Thus the needed identification in the constant-coefficient tower category does not require exactness of $\Delta_*$ on arbitrary $C_T$-module sheaves.

source.place: paragraph (2), construction and evaluation of the endomorphism e_bullet

proof.text: The varying-coefficient source identifications commute with evaluation by [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]; their restrictions do so by the same composition comparisons. Evaluate the constant-coefficient composite, using [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] for levelwise derived direct image. At level $n$ the class is the torsion diagonal class by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](4), the trace is $t_{p_i,n}$ by step 4, and restriction of the finite-coefficient equality of [det-sp-p1-trace](3) gives $e_{i,n}=\mathrm{id}$ in $D(P_{\mathrm{proet}},C_P)$. This last citation is explicitly a pro-etale finite-coefficient assertion; it is not an unproved transport of the ordinary etale identity.

source.place: paragraph (2), construction and evaluation of the endomorphism e_bullet

proof.text: The source and target of $e_{i,\bullet}$ are the system $A_{\bullet,P}$ in degree zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to the abelian category of system sheaves. It identifies $e_{i,\bullet}$ with a unique actual system-sheaf endomorphism. Such a morphism is a family commuting with the quotient transitions; equality is componentwise by the definition of that category. Apply the same degree-zero full faithfulness in the abelian category of $C_P$-module sheaves at each level: step 10 then says every actual component is the identity, hence $e_{i,\bullet}=\mathrm{id}$ already in the system derived category. Apply $R\varprojlim$. The natural direct-image/limit comparison [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] carries this composite to $\operatorname{Tr}_{p_i}\circ Rp_{i*}(\delta_{\Zl})$, since [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit](3) identifies $R\varprojlim c_\bullet$ with $\delta_{\Zl}$. Its source identification is the same one obtained by limiting the composition identification in step 9. Thus the composite is the identity after restriction to constant coefficients. The equivalence on complete objects [sk-lem-integral-models](1) is faithful, so the identity holds over the completed coefficient sheaf as claimed. Equality of arbitrary morphisms of derived systems was never inferred from their evaluated equalities: the degree-zero full faithfulness is essential here.

source.place: paragraph (2), degree-zero full faithfulness, equality of systems, then Rlim; Stacks 06XS(2)

All other retained citation statements agree with the current DAG. All non-elementary steps are below 2000 characters; no new nodes were needed.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–8 realize paragraph (1) and unit step 8: coherent section class, finite Cartier normalization, levelwise splitting, trace on systems, inverse limit, completeness, completed linearity, and actual reductions. Steps 9–11 realize paragraph (2) and unit step 9: supported source identification, finite integration, degree-zero equality of systems, and passage to the completed identity. tool_uses.why: Only the existing coherent Chern-class and twisted splitting interfaces are used; the item still proves the limit trace, its reductions and integration identities. This is the same tower-construction tool used by the blueprint.
The generic abelian and exact-evaluation structure of varying-coefficient towers is needed while forming the coherent class.
The generic levelwise direct-image theorem includes units and counits for varying coefficients; the unit has no such categorical theorem.
Canonical derived direct-image composition supplies scalar-restriction and p_i Delta identifications without replacing the geometric route.
The roots-of-unity transitions, reductions and completeness of the integral coefficient line are generic coefficient facts.
The generic epimorphic-tower theorem identifies the derived and ordinary limits on Y and P as well as W.
The item needs the projection-compatible Rlim comparison for towers over the discrete constant coefficient ring.
Generic identification of completed integral coefficients with the inverse limit of finite constant quotients.
The generic finite-reduction and completion-unit comparisons distinguish the constant and completed coefficient categories.
Only its completed-coefficient completeness and finite-reduction clauses are used; the constant-coefficient tower comparison is cited separately.
Checks the finite-perfect-quotient hypotheses of the completed direct-image tool.
The generic equivalence on complete objects provides unique linearity and faithfulness after restriction.
Generic exactness of closed direct image with quasi-compact complement identifies the supported source.
The generic degree-zero Hom identification is essential to equality of system morphisms.
Checks the Noetherian coefficient-ring hypothesis by the existing DVR/PID theorem with E=Q_l.

Generic derived reduction/restriction adjunction identifies actual tower projections with finite-reduction adjoints; it supplies a categorical tool, without replacing the projective-line geometric route.
